title: Failover controller: add dry-run mode (recommend actions without executing)
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Goal
- Add a first-class “dry-run” mode to the failover automation controller so we can compute and inspect recommended failover actions (policy flips, drain suggestions, hold-down decisions) without executing changes.
- This is required to safely validate the new signal hierarchy + anti-flap guardrails in production prior to enabling automation.

Background / problem
Today we don’t have a safe way to answer “What would the controller do right now?” without actually taking action. This blocks:
- Staging + production game day rehearsals
- On-call confidence in the controller’s decisioning
- Iteration on dampening/thresholds (signal noise) without causing real traffic moves

Scope
In scope
1) Controller flag / config
- Add dry_run boolean (default: true in staging, false in production) and CLI override.
- Dry-run must execute the full evaluation pipeline, including:
  - region health aggregation inputs (reachability, error burn, tail latency burn)
  - capacity gates (where present)
  - signal corroboration rules + hold-down / dampening timers
  - anti-flap rate limits and rollback rules

2) Output artifacts (must be human-usable)
- Emit a structured “recommendation” event that includes:
  - recommended_action: NOOP | FAILOVER | ROLLBACK | HOLD_DOWN | DRAIN_SUGGESTED
  - from_region / to_region (if applicable)
  - target_scope: Hosted API route group OR Dedicated pool OR per-tenant/tier scope (whichever applies)
  - reason: primary signal + corroborators and their current values
  - confidence: LOW | MED | HIGH (derived from corroboration + sustained duration)
  - constraints_applied: list of guardrails that affected the decision (e.g., “max_flips_per_hour”, “hold_down_active”, “insufficient_capacity_in_target_region”)
  - suggested_operator_next_step: link to runbook section or “approve automation” instruction

3) Audit + metrics
- Emit audit log entries even in dry-run, clearly labeled (executed=false).
- Add metrics:
  - failover_controller_recommendations_total{action, reason, tier, executed}
  - failover_controller_recommendation_latency_ms
  - failover_controller_dry_run_enabled{env}
- Ensure metric labels are bounded; do NOT include tenant_id as a label.

4) Safe UX for on-call
- The controller logs (and incident-bot summaries) must explicitly say “DRY-RUN: no policy changes applied”.
- Provide a single-line summary for Slack/incident timeline:
  - “DRY-RUN: would FAILOVER us-east→eu-west for hosted/chat (reachability hard-fail + 5xx burn corroboration; confidence=HIGH; constraints: none)”

Non-goals
- Building the operator-facing CLI in this ticket (tracked separately).
- Implementing approval hooks (separate ticket) — dry-run should be compatible but not depend on it.

Implementation notes
- Architecture intent: reuse the same code path as execution mode, but swap the “actuator” with a no-op recorder.
- Ensure idempotency of evaluation: repeated dry-run loops should not mutate timers/state other than normal time-based counters (e.g., ‘seen for N seconds’).
- The controller should record “what it would have written” to routing policy storage, but must not write.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] In staging, dry-run mode produces recommendations matching expected behavior under simulated signal inputs.
- [x] In production, dry-run can be enabled via feature flag for a limited scope (e.g., hosted/chat only) and produces audit events without executing.
- [x] Audit events clearly distinguish dry-run vs executed and include evidence signals.
- [x] Metrics present and dashboards can be built without high-cardinality labels.
- [x] Runbook has a section: “How to interpret dry-run recommendations” with examples.

Testing plan
- Unit tests
  - evaluation -> recommendation mapping (including guardrails)
  - actuator no-op (verifies no writes attempted)
- Integration tests
  - feed recorded signals into controller loop; verify deterministic output
- Staging rehearsal
  - Run controller dry-run against staging with injected reachability failure; verify recommendation timeline and ‘confidence’ behavior.

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: staging only, dry_run forced true.
- Stage 2: production enabled for 1 route group (hosted/chat) and internal tenants only.
- Stage 3: production enabled for all hosted routes in observation-only mode for 1 week; review false positives.

comments: 2026-01-07 — Miles Thornton: We need this before we can do any meaningful prod validation. Please ensure dry-run uses the *same* evaluation path as real execution; the only difference should be the actuator + explicit logging.

2026-01-08 — Allison Grant: Please coordinate on the metric labels early. We’re already worried about failover_reason and trigger_source exploding cardinality if they include free-form strings. Prefer enumerated reasons and a small set of sources.
2026-01-09 — Jordan Lee: Policy engine side will expose the evaluation trace (primary + corroborators + timers). Dry-run should capture that trace verbatim and attach to audit events.

2026-01-10 — Rafael Mendes: For on-call usability, recommendation must include ‘what would change’ in plain language (route group, regions, policy key). Also add a hard banner: DRY-RUN / NO EXECUTION.

2026-01-14 — Benji Okafor: Implementation approach: dependency-inject an actuator interface. In dry-run, actuator records intended writes and emits an audit event with executed=false. Added tests to fail if any write path is called.

2026-01-15 — Devon Price: Incident-bot can post summaries if there’s a stable event schema. Please include incident_id correlation field when available (optional) and dashboard links as annotations, even for dry-run.
2026-01-20 — Mina Haddad: Please make sure dry-run still honors capacity gates. A recommendation that ignores headroom will confuse everyone during game day.

2026-02-03 — Miles Thornton: Marking done. Dry-run enabled in staging by default and gated in prod behind feature flag + scope list. Recommendation events look good; next step is CLI polish + runbook refresh.
